ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare dispute with no refund: the rider's own pre-segment message authorised the reroute, so the off-route segment is exempt and the metered fare stands. No account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI ride, 18.0 km driven against 15.1 km optimal (+2.9 km) and 30.1 min against a 20.6 min estimate, charged $38.58 [F1][F2][F7]. RD-2 makes distance the refundable unit only for unexcused off-route segments on a metered trip, so everything turns on whether the single segment is exempt [RD-1][RD-2].

There is exactly one off-route segment, 12:27–12:35: 4.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, +2.16 km, up to 722 m off the corridor [F3]. Both advocates stipulate the ground for this segment as a general route choice by the rider, and RD-1 makes each segment the unit of review [F3][RD-1].

The rider's own message before the segment was a general route authorisation: the driver asked at 12:24 whether to take another way because the PIE jam was building, and the rider replied at 12:25 "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" — leaving the route to the driver for the sake of speed [F8][F9][F10]. That message is complete and timestamped, sent at 12:25, before the segment began at 12:27 [F10][F3][RD-5]. A general authorisation covers a route chosen to get to the destination, and the record shows no errand of the driver's own, no stop, and no loop that reaches nothing — no stop is measured in the segment and no driver-named detour place appears [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The rider's argument that the authorisation fails because the route was not in fact faster, read off the trip duration [F2], is not the test RD-5 sets: RD-5 defines the scope of a general authorisation by where the loop goes (an errand of the driver's own, a loop reaching nothing), not by a guarantee that the estimate is beaten; the presence of congestion on the corridor is corroborated, not contradicted, by the PIE speed band 2 record [F9][F2][F12][RD-5]. No RD-4 exemption is relied on, and none is available: there was no incident on the route, and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment [F14][F12][RD-4].

Because the segment is exempt, there is no unexcused extra kilometre to refund: the sum is Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) = 0 × $1.4098/km = $0.00, the rate being this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km ($4.06 ÷ 2.88 km) [F3][F4][RD-2]. The waiting item of $0.11 for 0.4 min is a metered waiting unit that the rider does not seek, and the total of $38.58 stands [F5][F7][RD-3]. The driver has no prior upheld route dispute, so no account flag arises [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint. The exchange concerns traffic and route choice; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is "none" [F8][F9][F11]. Evidence: the chat is complete and every message timestamped, the segment is measured, and the fare record supplies the rate, so the record settles every element this ruling needs [F10][F3][F4].

segment_findings.reason: The driver asked at 12:24 whether to take another way to avoid the building PIE jam [F8], and the rider replied at 12:25 "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间", a rider message sent before the segment started at 12:27 [F9][F10][F3]. This is a general route choice: the record shows no driver errand, no stop and no loop to nowhere in the segment [F3], so the route driven to reach the destination falls within the authorisation [RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The overall +2.9 km and +9.5 min against estimate [F1][F2] do not by themselves create a refund on a metered trip: RD-1 reviews each off-route segment and the only segment is exempt under the rider's own prior general authorisation [F3][F9][RD-1][RD-5].
The $4.06 excess-distance figure [F4] is refundable only for the extra_km of a non-exempt segment; the segment is exempt, so the refundable sum is 0 × $1.4098/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2].

Read in context, "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" is exactly the general route choice RD-5 contemplates, sent at 12:25 before the 12:27 segment start [F9][F10][F3][RD-5]; it is not a reason to make the segment count.

RD-5 defines a general authorisation's scope by where the loop goes (an errand of the driver's own or a loop reaching nothing), not by whether the estimate of 20.6 min was beaten; the 30.1 min duration [F2] with corridor congestion corroborated by the PIE speed band [F12] does not push the route outside the authorisation [F9][RD-5].

Correctly read, F14 and F12 close the RD-4 route, but RD-4 is not the exemption the driver relies on; the segment is exempt on the rider's prior consent, so the absence of an incident does not make it count [F14][F12][F9][RD-4][RD-5].
The driver's post-trip statement [F11] is not relied on as consent and adds nothing to the timestamped exchange; the consent rests on the rider's own pre-segment message [F9][F10][F11][RD-5].

The waiting item is $0.11 for 0.4 min on the metre [F5]; the rider seeks nothing on it and it does not affect the distance question, which is resolved by the segment being exempt [F5][F3][RD-3][RD-2].

The driver's own reading that no record ties the segment to a named road [F8][F9] confirms the finding of a general route choice, which is what makes the segment exempt; it does not require a named road for exemption [RD-5].
The PIE speed band 2 record [F12] is not and cannot be a standalone RD-4 exemption; the segment is exempt on prior rider consent instead [F12][F14][F9][RD-4][RD-5].
The driver's own concession that the record shows no errand, stop or loop to nowhere [F3] supports exemption of the segment, not a denial of it [RD-5].
